Question: Qiang drives \(15\) miles at an average speed of \(30\) miles per hour. How many additional miles will he have to drive at \(55\) miles per hour to average \(50\) miles per hour for the entire trip?
Solution:
Compare Qiang's progress with a trip at the desired \(50\) mph. His first \(15\) miles take \(15/30=\frac12\) hour. In that time, a \(50\)-mph trip would cover \(25\) miles, so he is \(10\) miles behind that target.

During the second part, he travels at \(55\) mph, gaining \(55-50=5\) miles per hour on the target pace. It takes \(10/5=2\) hours to make up the \(10\)-mile deficit. The additional distance is therefore

\[
55\cdot2=\boxed{110}\text{ miles},
\]

choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\). As a check, the full trip covers \(15+110=125\) miles in \(\frac12+2=2.5\) hours, giving \(125/2.5=50\) mph.
